newsitem.title: TURKEY: U.S. envoy says Iraq Kurds agree to extend truce.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy says Iraq Kurds agree to extend truce.

text.p: U.S. peace envoy Robert Pelletreau said on Thursday that two Iraqi Kurdish groups had agreed to extend permanently a ceasefire declared after two months of Kurdish infighting in northern Iraq.
"All particpants agree to maintain and strengthen the ceasefire within a permament context," Pelletreau told a news conference after talks in the Turkish capital.
Pelletreau brokered a ceasefire between the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) last week. The two sides began peace talks in Ankara on Wednesday.
The clashes gave Iraqi President Saddam Hussein a foothold in the Western-protected north of the country after a five-year hiatus.
The KDP joined forces with Baghdad in late August to take the key city of Arbil from the PUK, prompting U.S. missile strikes against targets in southern Iraq.
The KDP accuses Iran of backing the PUK militarily. Both PUK and Tehran deny this.
